meta.description: Skyfield apparent positions (light-time, gravitational deflection, aberration; no refraction) expressed in the true ecliptic and equinox of date.  lon/lat in degrees (lon 0-360 east of the true equinox of date), distance in km.
meta.timescale: load.timescale(builtin=True): Skyfield's bundled leap-second and delta-T tables (no download).  Time objects built from the ERFA TT two-part JD with ts.tt_jd(jd1, jd2); the UTC string is informational.
meta.method: lat, lon, dist = earth.at(t).observe(body).apparent().ecliptic_latlon(epoch='date'). Verified in skyfield/positionlib.py: ecliptic_latlon(epoch=...) with a non-None epoch calls _Fake(self, epoch).frame_latlon(framelib.ecliptic_frame); for epoch='date' the frame time is the position's own t.  framelib.ecliptic_frame is documented 'Reference frame of the true ecliptic and equinox of date' and its rotation is build_ecliptic_matrix(t) = rot_x(-(mean_obliquity(t.tdb) + d_eps)) @ t.M, where t.M = N @ P @ B (frame bias B, IAU 2006 precession P from Capitaine et al. 2003 4-angle formulation evaluated at TDB, nutation N from the full IAU 2000A series evaluated at TT) and d_eps is the IAU 2000A nutation in obliquity.  With epoch=None the J2000 ecliptic (ECLIPJ2000) is used instead; those values are the *_j2000_* fields.  apparent() applies light deflection by Sun(10), Jupiter(5) and Saturn(6) (599/699 fall back to the barycenters in de421), Earth deflection for a topocentric observer, then annual (and diurnal, for topocentric) aberration.

moon_topocentric_kochi.method: (earth + wgs84.latlon(9.9312, 76.2673, elevation_m=0.0)).at(t).observe(moon).apparent().ecliptic_latlon(epoch='date').  The observer's GCRS position uses Skyfield's builtin delta-T (skyfield_delta_t_s / skyfield_ut1_jd recorded per record) and no polar motion.
